gloss: to drain oil; to let oil drip off

definitions.gloss: to drain off oil; to let excess oil drip off fried food
definitions.explanation: A cooking technique where freshly fried food is placed on a rack or paper towel to allow excess oil to drip away, resulting in crispier and less greasy food.

examples.japanese: {揚|あ}げたら{油|あぶら}を{切|き}る。
キッチンペーパーの{上|うえ}で{油|あぶら}を{切|き}ってください。
examples.english: Please drain the oil on paper towels.

examples.japanese: {天|てん}ぷらは{油|あぶら}をしっかり{切|き}ると、サクサクに{仕上|しあ}がる。
examples.english: If you drain the oil thoroughly from tempura, it turns out crispy.

notes:
A fundamental cooking expression composed of {油|あぶら} (oil) + を (object marker) + {切|き}る (to cut). In this context, {切|き}る means to separate or remove rather than to cut with a blade. This step is essential in Japanese deep-frying ({揚|あ}げ{物|もの}) to achieve the prized crispy texture.

COMMON METHODS:
- {網|あみ}の{上|うえ}で{油|あぶら}を{切|き}る: drain on a wire rack
- キッチンペーパーで{油|あぶら}を{切|き}る: drain on paper towels
- {油切|あぶらき}り{網|あみ}: oil-draining rack

RELATED COOKING TERMS:
- {揚|あ}げる: to deep-fry
- {揚|あ}げ{物|もの}: deep-fried food
- {油|あぶら}{跳|は}ね: oil splattering
- {水|みず}を{切|き}る: to drain water — the same pattern applied to water (e.g., draining vegetables)
